learning: Iteration 0 failed on every track by drifting to 0.061 m early, so this iteration tests whether a wider sensor span, lower speed and a stronger, better-scaled steering law keep the robot on the line.
notes: Complete seven-sensor package on the Builder's iteration 1 geometry. The controller uses outer-weighted signal scaling, lower base_speed and a higher kp, to address the early off-track failure in iteration 0.
rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: all 60 trials ended off_track on every track, with max_error about 0.061 m, one line-loss event per run and progress of only 0.04 to 0.12. The robot leaves the line early and never recovers, so the first priority is keeping it on the line, not speed. Geometry follows the Builder's iteration 1 proposal: seven sensors at 10 mm pitch from x = -0.03 to +0.03 m at y = 0.04 m, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body_width 0.12 m (the off-track limit is 0.06 m regardless), mass 0.7 m, body_length 0.18 m. Controller: sensor_weights are the normalised sideways positions scaled to +/-1.5 at the outer sensors, [-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5], so the signal stays monotonic across the 0.03 m span and the outer sensors can respond before the line is lost. The lookahead is shorter (y = 0.04 m) than iteration 0 (y = 0.06 m), which the Builder moved to reduce phase lag, so kd is kept small (0.15) to damp without amplifying noise. kp is raised to 3.0 from 2.5 so a moderate offset produces enough correction on the narrower track (about 1050 PWM counts of wheel difference at a full signal of 1.0). ki is 0.05, a small value to remove any steady bias from the motor mismatch while keeping the integral well inside its +/-2 limit. base_speed is reduced to 1.4 from 1.8 because iteration 0 failed early, so lower speed gives the controller more time per bend; this still gives roughly 1.1 m/s at full throttle, and the Builder's feedback allows an increase later if completion is reached. line_loss is last_direction, as the baseline. Expected: fewer or no line-loss events and max_error below 0.06 m, with the first completions on the S-bend or oval if the lower speed and better sensing hold. Whether the speed is high enough for a 3 s finish is still untested.
